papers.title_en: LiveAct: Towards Real-Time Multi-Agent World Models with Heterogeneous Action Interfaces
papers.authors: Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Yue Ma, Zijie Meng, Teng Xi, Yuzhuo Chen, Yucheng Wang, Ruicheng Zhang, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Xiu Li, Fangneng Zhan
papers.evidence: 多智能体世界模型与异构动作接口
papers.tldr: 现有交互式视频世界模型多假设单一受控智能体与任务专用动作接口，难以统一生成多智能体未来。LiveAct以异构动作接口HAI为核心，用智能体感知空间调制绑定动作流与视觉实体，并以模式引导动作适配解释不同控制语义。模型经教师强制和推演感知分布匹配迁移到分块因果生成器，实现流式多智能体视频预测。在游戏与多机器人操作六类数据上，智能体归属准确率达0.898和0.942，512×448下达17.70 FPS。
papers.abstract_en: Interactive video world models predict how an environment evolves under user actions, but most existing systems assume one controlled agent and one task-specific action interface. We study multi-agent video world modeling, where one model generates a joint visual future for multiple controlled agents while interpreting heterogeneous controls ranging from binary game buttons to continuous robot commands. This task presents two complementary challenges. First, every agent-indexed action stream must control its intended visual entity independently. Second, the model must adapt the meaning of each control variable across different tasks, where the same tensor dimension may denote an attack, steering command, or robot command. We introduce LiveAct, centered on a Heterogeneous Action Interface (HAI) whose two components mirror this decomposition. To support independent control, Agent-Aware Spatial Modulation uses language-driven spatial gates and agent-specific attention to bind each action stream to its intended visual agent. To accommodate heterogeneous controls, Schema-Guided Action Adaptation describes each control variable in language and modulates its semantic token with the synchronized numerical value. We further transfer the complete interface to a blockwise causal generator through teacher forcing and rollout-aware distribution matching, enabling efficient streaming generation while retaining agent-specific control and action semantics. We instantiate the formulation on six multi-agent sources spanning games and multi-robot manipulation, and evaluate visual quality, action following, agent attribution, and latency. Across games and robot manipulation, LiveAct reaches 0.898 and 0.942 agent-attribution accuracy without agent locations or identity crops, and the causal generator attains 17.70 FPS at $512\times 448$.

papers.title_en: Design and Tuning of Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization
papers.evidence: 将进化优化用于多智能体系统设计
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统设计仍依赖人工经验，且候选架构评测成本高昂。本文提出贝叶斯进化优化框架，以进化算子生成多样化工作流图，并用图感知高斯过程与期望改进显式筛选高潜力候选。在BigCodeBench代码生成任务上，进化架构取得所评测智能体系统的最佳整体表现；在TabPFN表格预处理任务上，优化后的多智能体预处理在多个时序数据集优于默认模型，并在IID数据集保持竞争力。结果表明，贝叶斯选择能在昂贵评测预算下有效引导多智能体拓扑搜索。
papers.abstract_en: Designing effective multi-agent systems (MAS) remains a challenging and resource-intensive task. We propose a Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework for automatically discovering task-specific MAS topologies. The approach combines evolutionary operators to generate diverse workflow graphs with Bayesian optimization to focus cost intensive evaluations on promising candidates. In contrast to LLM-based candidate selection, our approach uses a graph-aware Gaussian Process and Expected Improvement to provide an explicit selection criterion during evolutionary search. We evaluate the method on BigCodeBench for code generation and on a tabular preprocessing benchmark using TabPFN. On BigCodeBench, evolved architectures achieve the highest overall performance among the evaluated agent systems. On temporal tabular datasets, optimized MAS preprocessing improves over the default TabPFN model on several tasks, while remaining competitive on IID datasets. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of Bayesian selection for guiding evolutionary MAS search under expensive evaluation budgets.
